question: Which of these is NOT solely dependent on money for keeping nurses happy in a hospital?

options.A: Supportive leadership and recognition
options.B: Basic monthly salary payment amounts
options.C: Overtime pay for extra shifts worked
options.D: Special hazard allowance additions

explanation: While good pay is essential, nurses also stay where they feel respected, appreciated, and supported by their bosses and team members! [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do mature red blood cells give up their nucleus and mitochondria?

options.A: To allow the cell to divide rapidly within the bloodstream
options.B: To prevent the cell from producing any metabolic waste
options.C: To ensure the cell can easily slip through lymphatic vessels
options.D: To make more room to carry oxygen inside the cell

explanation: That is correct! By clearing out internal clutter, the red blood cell has maximum interior space to pack in hemoglobin and carry as much oxygen as possible. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which two organs do the heaviest lifting when it comes to breaking down and removing hormones?

options.A: Pancreas and spleen
options.B: Lungs and skin
options.C: Liver and kidneys
options.D: Stomach and intestines

explanation: Your liver chemically alters and breaks down used hormones, while your kidneys filter the leftovers out into your urine. Great tag-team work! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why would an occupational health nurse test the hearing of workers in a noisy textile mill?

options.A: To identify early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it worsens
options.B: To check if employees are listening to unauthorized radio stations
options.C: To measure how fast the machinery is producing textile materials
options.D: To test the general intelligence and problem-solving skills of the staff

explanation: Loud factory noise can slowly damage hearing over time. Regular hearing tests (audiometry) help us catch any small changes early so we can protect the workers' ears. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h5)

question: Which test gives the final confirmation that a patient has active lung TB?

options.A: Physical auscultation of bilateral lung sounds
options.B: Routine complete blood count and electrolyte panel
options.C: Measurement of resting blood pressure and pulse rate
options.D: Sputum culture and acid-fast bacilli smear testing

explanation: Checking the patient's sputum for acid-fast bacilli or growing the germs in a lab gives the definitive proof needed to confirm active TB. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h4)

question: What tells you that an infant is ready to come out of Gallows traction?

options.A: The baby turns two years old
options.B: The ropes are starting to look worn out
options.C: X-rays show the bone has healed well with good callus formation
options.D: The parents ask for the metal frame to be taken down

explanation: We don't guess—we check! Only an X-ray proving the bone is strong enough will greenlight removing the traction. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why must personal distress be present alongside physical symptoms to diagnose female sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Physical symptoms alone always resolve spontaneously
options.B: Insurance companies will not pay for treatment otherwise
options.C: It proves the dysfunction is purely psychological
options.D: Some women experience variations in response without feeling bothered by them

explanation: Great thinking! Every body is different. What feels like a problem to one person might be completely normal and comfortable for another, which is why personal distress matters. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h1)

question: What does a high Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) level mostly point toward?

options.A: Severe acute viral hepatitis infection
options.B: Chronic kidney filtration failure
options.C: Bile duct obstruction or bone activity
options.D: Massive breakdown of red blood cells

explanation: Brilliant! ALP hangs out in the bile ducts and bones, so high numbers usually point your clinical suspicion toward biliary issues or bone growth/turnover. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T11#GNS221_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why is the patient told to hold their breath while the doctor inserts the needle?

options.A: To stop air from entering through the skin
options.B: To keep their blood pressure from dropping too low
options.C: To keep the diaphragm still so the liver doesn't get torn
options.D: To save oxygen in case they feel stressed

explanation: Correct! Holding the breath stops the chest and diaphragm from moving, keeping the liver completely still for a safe, clean needle entry. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h4)

question: What are the two main components that make up the cardiovascular system?

options.A: The brain and spinal cord
options.B: The heart and blood vessels
options.C: The lungs and airways
options.D: The kidneys and bladder

explanation: The cardiovascular system is composed of the heart, which acts as the pump, and blood vessels, which serve as the delivery pipes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal of encouraging student self-assessment in nursing education?

options.A: To allow students to assign their own final course grades.
options.B: To replace faculty-led clinical evaluations with student opinions.
options.C: To promote critical self-reflection and lifelong professional growth.
options.D: To reduce the workload of clinical instructors entirely.

explanation: Self-assessment helps you look at your own strengths and weaknesses so you can keep growing into an awesome, reflective nurse. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is a common local carbohydrate staple you will see in Nigerian menu planning?

options.A: Olive oil
options.B: Garri
options.C: Apples
options.D: Salmon

explanation: Garri, made from cassava, is a widely enjoyed and accessible energy source right here at home! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T005#GNS227_U3_T005_h2)

question: Why is daily foot care and inspection so crucial for patients with diabetes?

options.A: Daily observation increases blood circulation to the toes
options.B: Sweat buildup guarantees the rapid development of gangrene
options.C: Nerve damage can prevent them from feeling minor cuts or blisters
options.D: Skin color changes indicate the exact blood sugar level

explanation: Diabetes can cause nerve damage (neuropathy) in the feet, meaning minor sores can go unnoticed and turn into major wounds if not checked daily. Essential nursing wisdom! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h6)

question: Which type of fluid output is typically easiest to measure accurately in a hospital ward?

options.A: Urine collected in a graduated container
options.B: Moisture lost through normal breathing
options.C: Fluid lost from weeping skin wounds
options.D: Sweat lost during a mild afternoon fever

explanation: Urine can be easily captured and measured using marked collection containers or catheter drainage bags. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h4)

question: When taking off your personal protective equipment (doffing), which item should come off FIRST?

options.A: Gloves
options.B: Isolation gown
options.C: Respirator mask
options.D: Face shield

explanation: Spot on! Your gloves are the dirtiest item since they touched the patient directly, so peeling them off first keeps the rest of your cleanup process safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the recommended minimum time for brushing teeth properly?

options.A: Two full minutes
options.B: Five exact minutes
options.C: Thirty total seconds
options.D: Ten brief seconds

explanation: Brushing for at least two minutes gives you enough time to reach all tooth surfaces and get rid of stubborn plaque. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why do older adults need a good amount of protein relative to their body weight?

options.A: To prevent the rapid buildup of visceral fat around internal organs
options.B: To counteract age-related muscle loss and support immune function
options.C: To provide extra calories for increased daily physical activity
options.D: To compensate for faster breakdown of protein in the kidneys

explanation: Exactly! Higher protein helps older adults fight off muscle wasting (sarcopenia) and keeps their immune system strong. Simple and vital! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T014#GNS227_U2_T014_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing consideration related to postpartum endocrine changes?

options.A: Monitoring for sudden increases in maternal blood pressure caused by rising placental hormone levels
options.B: Observing for successful milk let-down reflex stimulated by infant suckling and oxytocin
options.C: Reassuring the mother about normal physiological changes during her hospital recovery
options.D: Assessing for signs of postpartum mood changes linked to rapid estrogen and progesterone withdrawal

explanation: Placental hormone levels drop rapidly after delivery, not rise. Therefore, rising placental hormone levels are not a concern postpartum. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h6)

question: What usually happens to a patient's pulse rate when their body temperature goes up?

options.A: The heart rate goes down
options.B: The pulse becomes weak and irregular
options.C: The heart rate stays completely normal
options.D: The heart rate goes up

explanation: Correct! As body temperature climbs, the metabolism speeds up, making the heart beat faster too. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why must you check a patient's blood pressure before giving them a drug that lowers blood pressure?

options.A: To test if the automatic cuff machine is working properly
options.B: To satisfy routine paperwork requirements set by the hospital
options.C: To make sure the blood pressure is not already dangerously low
options.D: To calculate how much water the patient drank that morning

explanation: If their blood pressure is already very low, giving the pill could cause them to faint or crash. Always check your parameters first! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h4)

question: When opening a sterile pack, which part of the sterile drape or wrapper is always considered contaminated?

options.A: The portion closest to the patient
options.B: The top surface facing upwards
options.C: The outer one-inch border
options.D: The exact center of the drape

explanation: Spot on! That outer edge touches non-sterile surfaces when packaged, so we always treat the outer one-inch margin as unsterile. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h6)

question: How does teamwork between nurses, doctors, and pharmacists improve the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: By removing the need for any internal hospital quality audits
options.B: By allowing nurses to take over surgical operations from physicians
options.C: By shifting all financial responsibilities entirely onto patients
options.D: By combining different professional skills to prevent drug errors and waste

explanation: Spot on! When healthcare professionals team up, they catch mistakes early and keep patients safe. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main job of a midwife in a primary health care clinic?

options.A: Managing normal pregnancies and conducting safe deliveries
options.B: Treating chronic heart diseases in elderly patients
options.C: Performing routine dental extractions for children
options.D: Managing hospital financial accounts and budgets

explanation: You nailed it! Midwives are experts at caring for women through pregnancy and labor, ensuring both mother and baby come through safely. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is a common physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Diabetes mellitus
options.B: Drinking adequate water
options.C: Regular aerobic exercise
options.D: Eating fresh fruits daily

explanation: Chronic conditions like diabetes damage blood vessels and nerves over time, making it a major physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h3)

question: How can severe physical or emotional stress lead to spaced-out periods (oligomenorrhoea)?

options.A: By suppressing hypothalamic release of GnRH
options.B: By causing immediate scarring of the uterine wall
options.C: By destroying ovarian follicles directly
options.D: By blocking estrogen receptors in the liver

explanation: Stress triggers hormones like cortisol, which temporarily puts a pause on the hypothalamus releasing GnRH. Without that signal, ovulation gets delayed! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h3)

question: If a patient vomits something that looks like coffee grounds, what does that usually mean?

options.A: Partially digested blood from the stomach
options.B: A complete blockage of the large intestine
options.C: The recent consumption of dark roasted coffee
options.D: Excessive production of normal bile fluid

explanation: Classic clinical sign! Stomach acid reacts with bleeding in the upper GI tract, giving old blood that distinct coffee-ground texture. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h6)

question: Why is it super important for a patient to stay completely still during a CT scan?

options.A: Motion blurs the images and requires a repeat scan
options.B: Moving triggers an emergency shutdown of the scanner
options.C: Movement can cause the motorized table to break
options.D: Patient movement stops the release of contrast dye

explanation: Movement messes up the computer's picture, making the scan blurry and useless. Staying still helps get it right the first time! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common home hazard that frequently leads to patient falls?

options.A: Bright lighting in bedroom hallways
options.B: Grab bars installed inside showers
options.C: Low-pile wall-to-wall carpeting
options.D: Loose scatter rugs on slick floors

explanation: Loose rugs easily slip underfoot or catch assistive device tips, making them a major tripping hazard in homes. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the largest and least compressible part of the foetal body during birth?

options.A: The shoulders
options.B: The trunk
options.C: The head
options.D: The pelvis

explanation: The foetal skull is the largest part of the infant body and requires careful passage through the pelvis during delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h1)

question: Why is it vital to educate family members about the fluid chart when they are visiting?

options.A: Family members must empty the bedpans during visiting hours
options.B: Education keeps visitors from drinking the patient's water
options.C: Visitors often give the patient drinks that need to be recorded
options.D: Visitors are legally required to sign off on the hospital chart

explanation: Family members frequently bring water, juice, or tea, and nurses must capture these amounts to keep the record accurate. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h8)

question: Why does a cut or infected area of skin suddenly become red, warm, and swollen?

options.A: Pathogens are multiplying rapidly and blocking normal blood flow
options.B: Lymphocytes are actively producing antibodies inside the tissue
options.C: Stomach acid and tears are leaking into the subcutaneous tissue
options.D: Blood vessels dilate to bring white blood cells to the site

explanation: Spot on! That redness and warmth are signs of your body sending extra blood carrying rescue white blood cells straight to the battleground to fight the infection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient turns yellowish and has severe upper belly pain after mixing local herbs with paracetamol for weeks. What likely happened?

options.A: Drug-induced liver injury from combined metabolic toxicity
options.B: A complete blockage of the urinary tract by solid crystals
options.C: Sudden infection caused by drinking too much cold water daily
options.D: A normal, expected side effect of taking harmless herbal teas

explanation: The liver has to process everything we swallow. Combining heavy doses of drugs and potent herbal mixes overworks the liver and can cause serious damage. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h3)

question: A family caregiver is exhausted and needs a short break to run errands. Which hospice team member is best suited to sit with the patient during this time?

options.A: A medical social worker
options.B: A registered nurse
options.C: A hospice volunteer
options.D: A certified nursing assistant

explanation: Volunteers frequently provide companionship and respite care, giving family caregivers time away to rest or attend to personal errands. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h4)

question: How does community mobilisation directly support primary health care goals?

options.A: By building large tertiary teaching hospitals in every small town
options.B: By stopping patients from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.C: By helping people manage preventable diseases and improve local sanitation
options.D: By replacing community health workers with paid international staff

explanation: Primary health care focuses on prevention and community-level action, which mobilisation directly achieves. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main difference between normal grief and complicated grief?

options.A: Normal grief requires heavy psychiatric medication
options.B: Normal grief has no sadness, only anger and frustration
options.C: Complicated grief remains intense and paralyzing for six months or longer
options.D: Complicated grief only happens after sudden accidental deaths

explanation: While normal grief slowly softens over time, complicated grief stays severe and keeps a person from functioning well past the six-month mark. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h3)

question: Which germ is the most common culprit behind fungal pneumonia in patients with advanced HIV?

options.A: Pneumocystis jirovecii
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Cryptococcus neoformans
options.D: Candida albicans

explanation: Spot on! Pneumocystis jirovecii loves to strike when the immune system is deeply weakened, causing a serious type of pneumonia. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T3#GNS216_U6_T3_h3)

question: A cook uses the same board to chop raw chicken and slice fresh tomatoes without washing it. What safety rule did they break?

options.A: Cook food to high pressures
options.B: Separate raw and cooked food
options.C: Keep food at safe temperatures
options.D: Keep the drying area ventilated

explanation: Classic cross-contamination! Always wash your boards and knives between raw meats and ready-to-eat foods to keep germs from spreading. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h6)

question: What kind of muscle weakness or paralysis is typical in polio?

options.A: Flaccid paralysis
options.B: Decerebrate paralysis
options.C: Rigid paralysis
options.D: Spastic paralysis

explanation: Spot on! When lower motor neurons are destroyed, the muscles lose their tone and become limp and floppy—this is known as flaccid paralysis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h2)

question: How does adrenaline directly affect blood flow to the uterus when a mum is stressed?

options.A: It stops all electrical activity in the myometrium instantly
options.B: It dilates blood vessels to increase oxygen delivery to the fetus
options.C: It converts glucose into amniotic fluid rapidly
options.D: It constricts blood vessels and reduces blood flow to the uterus

explanation: Stress hormones cause blood vessels to tighten up (vasoconstriction), drawing blood away from the womb and sending it to the big muscles instead. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h2)

question: Why must a nurse check for an official agency registration number on a drug before giving it?

options.A: To determine which pharmaceutical company manufactured the raw chemical compound
options.B: To calculate the exact wholesale profit margin for the hospital pharmacy
options.C: To ensure the medication qualifies for international shipping exemptions
options.D: To confirm that the drug has been evaluated for safety, quality, and efficacy

explanation: That registration number is your safety green light! It tells you NFDAC or the relevant body has tested the drug and approved it for use. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why are recreational play breaks important alongside structured classroom lessons?

options.A: They allow teachers to grade papers without student interruptions
options.B: They provide a necessary mental break to refresh student focus
options.C: They ensure students never feel tired during school hours
options.D: They completely replace the need for physical education curricula

explanation: Brief periods of unstructured play reduce mental fatigue, helping students return to class more attentive and ready to learn. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main job of the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: To connect the central nervous system to the rest of the body
options.B: To produce vital brain chemicals
options.C: To store long-term memories in the brain
options.D: To protect the delicate spinal cord from physical injury

explanation: You got it! Think of the peripheral nervous system as the network of highways carrying messages back and forth between your brain/spinal cord and your limbs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of the mucus layer inside your gut?

options.A: To produce digestive enzymes that break down dietary fats
options.B: To absorb complex carbohydrates straight into your bloodstream
options.C: To speed up how fast waste moves through the colon
options.D: To trap bicarbonate and protect your stomach cells from harsh acid

explanation: Think of mucus as a protective shield! It holds bicarbonate right against your stomach lining to neutralize strong digestive acids so they don't harm your cells. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h1)

question: Approximately what percentage of a person's vulnerability to addiction is typically attributed to genetics?

options.A: Nearly 100 percent
options.B: Around 10 percent
options.C: About 50 percent
options.D: Less than 5 percent

explanation: Twin and family studies consistently show that genetic predisposition accounts for about half of a person's risk for developing an addiction. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h4)

question: A cancer patient on chemo has a fever of 38.5°C and a very low neutrophil count. What is your immediate priority action?

options.A: Wait for routine morning blood cultures to return before calling the physician.
options.B: Administer prescribed broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics immediately.
options.C: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold citrus juices.
options.D: Apply an ice blanket to bring down the patient's core body temperature.

explanation: Safety first! Febrile neutropenia is a life-threatening emergency. Quick IV antibiotics are vital to stop rapid-fire sepsis in its tracks. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h6)

question: What triggers the release of the hormone cholecystokinin (CCK) during digestion?

options.A: The drop in pH inside the stomach lumen
options.B: The presence of fats and proteins in the duodenum
options.C: The smell of food before it enters the mouth
options.D: The arrival of water in the large intestine

explanation: When fats and proteins hit the first part of your small intestine (duodenum), CCK gets released. It tells the gallbladder to squeeze out bile and the pancreas to release its enzymes! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting quality improvement reviews in a rehab facility?

options.A: To identify safety risks and find ways to improve patient care outcomes
options.B: To increase the cost of hospital admission fees
options.C: To find individual staff members to punish for making mistakes
options.D: To reduce the number of therapy hours required by insurance

explanation: Spot on! Quality improvement is all about making systems safer and patient care better—it's never about assigning blame. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h8)

question: What is the main job of endocrine glands in our body?

options.A: Filtering waste products out of liquid blood
options.B: Secreting hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes for the stomach
options.D: Pumping oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: Spot on! Endocrine glands don't use ducts. They release their chemical messengers (hormones) straight into nearby blood vessels to reach organs all over the body. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h1)

question: A nurse uses a dietary assessment to establish a baseline. What does this mean for patient care?

options.A: It provides a starting point to measure future nutritional changes and treatment progress
options.B: It acts as a permanent record that cannot be altered during the hospital stay
options.C: It proves that the patient has no underlying metabolic diseases
options.D: It serves as the final clearance for the patient to be discharged home

explanation: Establishing a baseline gives healthcare providers a reference point to see if interventions are helping or if the patient's condition is worsening. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h2)

question: What is the main goal of tertiary prevention for someone living with COPD?

options.A: Slowing down the disease and preventing troublesome complications
options.B: Preventing airway inflammation back when they were a child
options.C: Screening healthy family members for hidden lung issues
options.D: Completely curing the permanent damage in the air sacs

explanation: Tertiary prevention steps in after a chronic illness is already present. The aim is to help the patient manage symptoms, stay active, and avoid severe flare-ups. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h6)

question: A patient becomes dizzy and nauseated shortly after taking a sublingual tablet. What unique advantage of this route can the nurse utilize?

options.A: Give a large glass of milk to neutralize the medicine.
options.B: Instruct the patient to spit out any remaining undissolved medication.
options.C: Wait for the liver to filter out the toxic portion.
options.D: Pump the patient's stomach immediately to remove the drug.

explanation: Because absorption happens in the mouth, removing unabsorbed medication can stop further entry into the blood. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h4)

question: What mask must you wear when entering a room under droplet precautions?

options.A: Double sterile surgical gloves
options.B: A full body hazardous materials suit
options.C: A fitted N95 respirator mask
options.D: A standard surgical or medical mask

explanation: Correct! A simple surgical mask does a great job blocking those heavy respiratory droplets from landing in your nose and mouth. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the final step after completing a community situation analysis?

options.A: Closing down the primary health center for renovations
options.B: Translating the findings into an actionable health plan
options.C: Waiting for another NGO to come and do the work
options.D: Destroying all survey papers to protect patient privacy

explanation: The entire purpose of gathering and analyzing situation data is to guide practical healthcare planning and intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why do infectious disease outbreaks often require international teamwork?

options.A: Infectious diseases easily cross national borders and spread globally
options.B: International agencies hold the patent on all known antibiotics
options.C: Local hospitals refuse to treat contagious patients
options.D: National governments lack any interest in stopping local outbreaks

explanation: Viruses and bacteria don't check passports at the border! Because germs spread fast across countries, countries must work together to stop pandemics. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which receptors does norepinephrine target to keep the penis in a flaccid state?

options.A: Beta-2 adrenergic receptors
options.B: Nicotinic cholinergic receptors
options.C: Alpha-1 adrenergic receptors
options.D: Muscarinic cholinergic receptors

explanation: Keep it up! Norepinephrine binds to alpha-1 receptors on the smooth muscles, making them contract and keep blood flow low. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T4#GNS121_U4_T4_h3)

question: What main feature separates hospital waste from ordinary rubbish at home?

options.A: It always smells much worse than domestic garbage
options.B: It is generated only by medical doctors and surgeons
options.C: It can be recycled directly without prior processing
options.D: It contains biological, chemical, and radioactive hazards

explanation: You got this! Healthcare waste needs special care because it carries dangerous germs and materials that can cause disease or injury—unlike normal house trash. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the official definition of reproductive health according to the broader health context?

options.A: The total absence of sexually transmitted infections in an adult population
options.B: A government program aimed at controlling population growth rates
options.C: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters of the reproductive system
options.D: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help

explanation: Reproductive health covers total physical, mental, and social wellness regarding the reproductive system, rather than just lacking disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h1)

question: A patient comes to the emergency ward bleeding heavily from an unsafe abortion. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Provide immediate lifesaving emergency care to stabilize the patient
options.B: Report the patient to the police before offering any medical treatment
options.C: Wait for a court order before administering intravenous fluids
options.D: Refuse care based on personal moral objections to abortion

explanation: Saving a life always comes first! As a nurse, your duty is to stabilize and treat your patient in an emergency, no matter the circumstances. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: What defines an immunization 'defaulter' child?

options.A: A child who experienced a severe allergic reaction to a vaccine
options.B: A child who completed all required immunizations ahead of time
options.C: A child who received an initial dose but missed subsequent scheduled doses
options.D: A child who has never received any vaccine at all

explanation: A defaulter started their immunization schedule but failed to return for booster or subsequent doses on time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: What is the main goal of doing a home visit when assessing family vulnerability?

options.A: To search the house for stolen property
options.B: To check out environmental hazards and living conditions firsthand

question: In public health, what age group is generally referred to as adolescents?

options.A: 20 to 30 years
options.B: 5 to 9 years
options.C: 10 to 19 years
options.D: 35 to 50 years

explanation: Spot on! The World Health Organization defines adolescence as the teenage years spanning from 10 to 19 years of age. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which eye finding is most often seen in a patient with poorly controlled high blood pressure?

options.A: Drusen under the macula
options.B: Sticky pus from the conjunctiva
options.C: Cloudy protein clumps in the lens
options.D: Flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages

explanation: You nailed it! High pressure can strain tiny retinal blood vessels until they burst, creating little flame-shaped bleeds that show up during an eye exam. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T4#GNS311_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of the foramen ovale in a baby's heart before birth?

options.A: Connecting the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava to bypass the liver
options.B: Allowing blood to flow from the right atrium directly into the left atrium
options.C: Preventing maternal blood cells from entering the foetal heart chambers
options.D: Directing deoxygenated blood from the upper body back to the placenta

explanation: Spot on! The foramen ovale is a little flap-like door between the heart's upper chambers that lets oxygen-rich blood skip the right ventricle and lungs. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T005#GNS226_U2_T005_h5)

question: Which level of prevention stops risk factors from even starting through broad social and economic policies?

options.A: Clinical rehabilitation
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Primordial prevention is all about stopping risk factors before they even take root in a society through broad policies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is polypharmacy generally defined as?

options.A: Stopping all medications abruptly without advice
options.B: Taking five or more medications concurrently
options.C: Injecting a single drug twice a day
options.D: Using only traditional herbs for chronic illnesses

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to the use of multiple drugs at the same time, commonly set at a threshold of five or more. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is capillary bleeding usually less dangerous than arterial bleeding?

options.A: Capillary blood carries no oxygen
options.B: Capillaries carry blood under very low pressure, causing a slow ooze
options.C: Capillaries only exist in the dead outer skin layer
options.D: The body instantly clots capillaries without platelets

explanation: Because tiny capillaries have very low pressure, any bleeding from them usually trickles slowly rather than gushing out fast. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of public health nursing compared to traditional hospital bedside nursing?

options.A: Performing major surgical procedures independently
options.B: Prescribing advanced medications for rare conditions
options.C: Protecting and promoting the health of entire populations
options.D: Managing hospital budgets and medical equipment

explanation: Public health nursing looks past the single patient to protect whole communities and prevent illness at a macro level. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is the big difference between bactericidal and bacteriostatic drugs?

options.A: Bactericidal agents require acidic pH, while bacteriostatic agents need alkaline pH
options.B: Bacteriostatic drugs work only in the lungs, while bactericidal drugs work everywhere
options.C: Bactericidal drugs kill bacteria, whereas bacteriostatic drugs stop their growth
options.D: Bacteriostatic drugs destroy human cells, but bactericidal drugs protect them

explanation: Easy to remember: Bacterici-DAL drugs outright KILL the bacteria, while bacteriostatic drugs just press 'pause' on their growth and let your immune system finish the job! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is your very first action if a surgical drain accidentally falls completely out of a patient's wound?

options.A: Try to gently push the same tube right back into the hole
options.B: Leave the open wound uncovered so fresh air can dry it out
options.C: Cover the open site with a sterile dressing and notify the doctor
options.D: Wash the fallen tube with soap and tape it back onto the skin

explanation: Never try to push a fallen drain back in—that introduces germs! Instead, cover the site with a sterile dressing right away and call the doctor. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h6)
